note: Quoted from Harris (1966). Harris states explicitly that he was unable to examine Wasmann's specimens, so this entry can retain only the soldier account and measurements of Wasmann (1911) and the nomenclatural treatment by Snyder & Emerson (1949); units millimetres.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: In the key it is distinguished from A. microdens (left mandible with only 1 median marginal tooth) and the other species of the genus by the 2 very small marginal teeth on the left mandible of the major soldier and the head length including mandibles of 1.8—2.0 mm. A series of soldiers and workers from the Congo was identified by Wasmann (1911) as Termes cavithorax, but he noted at the same time that the mandibles of the major soldier are "strongly curved and sharp, the right mandible without teeth, the left mandible with 2 very small teeth at the middle, the posterior tooth visible only under magnification", which does not agree with Sjöstedt's description; on this basis Snyder & Emerson (1949) established these specimens as the new species wasmanni, without further discussion. Harris (1966) was unable to examine this material, so the morphological data for the species remain limited to Wasmann's original account.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Measurements given by Wasmann (mm): total body length, major soldier 4.0—4.3, minor soldier 2.5—3.6; head length including mandibles, major soldier 1.8—2.0, minor soldier 1.2—1.6. Type locality Sankuru, Congo.
